solution.explanation: The O–CH₃ bond breaks (the O–aryl bond has partial double bond character), so the products are phenol and methyl iodide: C₆H₅OCH₃ + HI → C₆H₅OH + CH₃I.
solution.why_others_wrong: 20.4 g is 0.10 mol of iodobenzene, which is not formed. 9.4 g is the mass of phenol, the other product. 7.1 g halves the moles.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', reactions of ethers (cleavage of C–O bond)
solution.final_answer: Option A: 14.2 g

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Nitration of benzaldehyde gives mainly o- and p-nitrobenzaldehyde.
Statement II: Bromination of benzoic acid in the presence of FeBr₃ gives mainly p-bromobenzoic acid.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Both –CHO and –COOH are electron-withdrawing, deactivating and meta-directing. Nitration of benzaldehyde gives m-nitrobenzaldehyde, and bromination of benzoic acid gives m-bromobenzoic acid.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', electrophilic substitution reactions
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The addition of HCN to ethanal is catalysed by a base.
Reason (R): The base converts HCN into the cyanide ion, a stronger nucleophile, which adds readily to the carbonyl carbon.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: With pure HCN the reaction is very slow. A base generates CN⁻, which is a much stronger nucleophile than HCN; it attacks the carbonyl carbon, and the alkoxide formed takes a proton from HCN to give the cyanohydrin.
steps: A: base catalyses the reaction → true
R: base gives CN⁻, the stronger nucleophile → true
That is why the base speeds up the addition → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', nucleophilic addition (addition of HCN)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Each reagent in List-I reacts with a carbonyl compound, >C=O. Match it with the group formed in the product (List-II).

List-I:
A. Hydrazine, NH₂NH₂
B. Phenylhydrazine, C₆H₅NHNH₂
C. Semicarbazide, NH₂CONHNH₂
D. Hydroxylamine, NH₂OH

List-II:
I. >C=N–OH
II. >C=N–NH–CO–NH₂
III. >C=N–NH₂
IV. >C=N–NH–C₆H₅

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Ammonia derivatives Z–NH₂ condense with the carbonyl group, losing water, to give >C=N–Z: hydrazone (Z = NH₂), phenylhydrazone (Z = NHC₆H₅), semicarbazone (Z = NHCONH₂) and oxime (Z = OH).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', reactions with ammonia and its derivatives
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about carboxylic acids and their derivatives are correct?

(a) Carboxylic acids react with PCl₃ to give acyl chlorides.
(b) Nitriles are hydrolysed, through amides, to carboxylic acids in the presence of H⁺ or OH⁻.
(c) Carboxylic acids react with alkalis but not with metals such as sodium.
(d) Esterification of a carboxylic acid with an alcohol is an irreversible reaction.
(e) Acyl chlorides and acid anhydrides are hydrolysed by water to give carboxylic acids.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Preparation and reactions of carboxylic acids
solution.explanation: NCERT: acids give acyl chlorides with PCl₅, PCl₃ or SOCl₂; nitriles are hydrolysed to amides and then to acids; acids react with electropositive metals (liberating H₂) as well as with alkalis; esterification is reversible, so water is removed to shift the equilibrium; acyl chlorides and anhydrides are hydrolysed to acids.
steps: (c) they react with Na too (H₂ evolved) → false
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option includes (c) or (d), both false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', methods of preparation and chemical reactions of carboxylic acids
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b) and (e) only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
How many of the following can undergo self aldol condensation in the presence of dilute alkali?
Ethanal, propanone, methanal, benzaldehyde, 2,2-dimethylpropanal, acetophenone, propanal

solution.concept: Requirement of an α-hydrogen for aldol condensation
solution.explanation: Aldol condensation needs at least one α-hydrogen, which the base removes to form the carbanion (enolate). Methanal and benzaldehyde have no α-carbon bearing hydrogen; in 2,2-dimethylpropanal, (CH₃)₃C–CHO, the α-carbon carries no hydrogen.
steps: α-H present: ethanal, propanone, acetophenone (CH₃ group), propanal
solution.why_others_wrong: 3 usually misses acetophenone, whose methyl group supplies α-hydrogens. 5 counts 2,2-dimethylpropanal, whose α-carbon is quaternary. 7 counts every carbonyl compound.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', aldol condensation
solution.final_answer: Option B: 4

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
How many of the following are stronger acids than phenol?
Ethanol, p-nitrophenol, o-cresol, picric acid (2,4,6-trinitrophenol), water, m-nitrophenol, p-cresol

solution.concept: Effect of substituents on the acidity of phenol
solution.explanation: Electron-withdrawing –NO₂ groups stabilise the phenoxide ion and increase acidity (pKa: p-nitrophenol 7.1, m-nitrophenol 8.3, picric acid 0.71, against phenol 10.0). Electron-releasing –CH₃ groups decrease it (cresols pKa about 10.2). Ethanol (15.9) and water are weaker acids than phenol.
solution.why_others_wrong: 2 leaves out m-nitrophenol (–NO₂ still withdraws electrons by −I at the meta position). 4 or 5 count a cresol, whose methyl group makes it a weaker acid than phenol.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', acidity of phenols (pKa table)
solution.final_answer: Option C: 3

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Compound X, C₅H₁₀O, does not reduce Tollens' reagent but gives a yellow precipitate with iodine and NaOH. On Clemmensen reduction, X gives n-pentane. X is:

solution.concept: Identifying a carbonyl compound from its tests
solution.explanation: No Tollens' test → a ketone, not an aldehyde. Iodoform test → a CH₃CO– group. Clemmensen reduction gives the alkane with the same carbon skeleton, so the chain must be unbranched.
solution.why_others_wrong: Pentan-3-one has no CH₃CO– group, so it gives no iodoform. 3-Methylbutan-2-one gives 2-methylbutane, not n-pentane. Pentanal is an aldehyde and reduces Tollens' reagent.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', chemical reactions (Clemmensen reduction, haloform reaction, Tollens' test)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Pentan-2-one

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about ethers are correct?

(a) Anisole reacts with CH₃Cl and anhydrous AlCl₃ to give mainly 2- and 4-methoxytoluene.
(b) Nitration of anisole gives mainly 2- and 4-nitroanisole.
(c) In the cleavage of ethers, the order of reactivity of the hydrogen halides is HI > HBr > HCl.
(d) Ethers are prepared in good yield by heating tertiary alcohols with concentrated H₂SO₄ at 413 K.
(e) Molecules of methoxymethane form hydrogen bonds with one another, like those of ethanol.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The –OCH₃ group activates the ring and directs to ortho and para positions (Friedel–Crafts, nitration). NCERT gives the order HI > HBr > HCl for cleavage. Acid dehydration of tertiary alcohols gives alkenes, because elimination competes. Ethers have no O–H, so they cannot hydrogen bond with one another.
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option includes (d) or (e), both false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', ethers (preparation, physical and chemical properties)
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In the acid-catalysed dehydration of ethanol to ethene, the first step is protonation of the oxygen atom of the alcohol.
Statement II: The last step of this mechanism is the loss of a water molecule from the carbocation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Mechanism of acid-catalysed dehydration of alcohols
solution.explanation: Step 1: protonation of the alcohol to give the oxonium ion. Step 2: loss of water to give the carbocation (the slowest, rate-determining step). Step 3: loss of a proton from the carbocation to give the alkene.
steps: Statement I: protonation is step 1 → true
Statement II: water is lost in step 2; step 3 is loss of H⁺ → false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', dehydration of alcohols (mechanism)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Phenol is a weaker acid than ethanoic acid.
Reason (R): In the ethanoate ion the negative charge is delocalised over two electronegative oxygen atoms, whereas in the phenoxide ion it is delocalised over the less electronegative carbon atoms of the ring.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Relative acidity of carboxylic acids and phenols
solution.explanation: The carboxylate ion has two equivalent resonance structures with the negative charge on oxygen, so it is much more stabilised than phenoxide, where the canonical structures place the charge on ring carbons. The more stable conjugate base means the stronger acid.
steps: Stability of the conjugate base decides acidity → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', acidity of carboxylic acids
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The amine (CH₃)₃C–NH₂ (2-methylpropan-2-amine) is classified as a:

solution.explanation: Amines are classified by the number of hydrogen atoms of NH₃ replaced by alkyl or aryl groups, not by the nature of the carbon bearing the nitrogen. Here only one H is replaced (by a tert-butyl group), so it is a primary amine.
steps: N bonded to one carbon group and two H atoms
(The carbon attached to N is tertiary, but that does not decide the class of an amine)
solution.why_others_wrong: Secondary and tertiary amines have two and three carbon groups on nitrogen. A quaternary ammonium compound has four groups on a positively charged nitrogen.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', structure and classification of amines
solution.final_answer: Option C: primary amine

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 9.3 g of aniline is diazotised. The diazonium salt is converted into its fluoroborate, which is treated with aqueous sodium nitrite in the presence of copper powder, so that the diazo group is replaced by –NO₂. Assuming every step is complete, the mass of nitrobenzene formed is (C = 12, H = 1, N = 14, O = 16):

solution.concept: Replacement of the diazo group by a nitro group
solution.explanation: C₆H₅NH₂ → C₆H₅N₂⁺ → C₆H₅N₂⁺BF₄⁻ → (NaNO₂, Cu) C₆H₅NO₂ + N₂. Every step is 1 : 1.
solution.why_others_wrong: 10.3 g is 0.10 mol of benzonitrile (the CuCN product). 15.7 g is 0.10 mol of bromobenzene. 6.2 g halves the moles.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', reactions of diazonium salts (replacement by nitro group)
solution.final_answer: Option A: 12.3 g

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Amines behave as Lewis bases because:

options.text: they contain hydrogen atoms bonded to nitrogen
nitrogen is more electronegative than carbon
the nitrogen atom has an unshared pair of electrons

solution.explanation: The lone pair on nitrogen can be donated to an electron-pair acceptor such as H⁺ (forming R–NH₃⁺) or a Lewis acid. That is what makes amines bases.
steps: Nitrogen in amines: three bonds + one lone pair
Lone pair donated to H⁺ → ammonium ion
solution.why_others_wrong: Tertiary amines have no N–H bond yet are bases. The electronegativity of N and water solubility do not by themselves make a compound a base (higher amines are insoluble but still basic).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', chemical reactions (basic character of amines)
solution.final_answer: Option D: the nitrogen atom has an unshared pair of electrons

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Primary amines have lower boiling points than alcohols of comparable molecular mass.
Statement II: Methanamine reacts with benzoyl chloride to give N-methylbenzamide.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The N–H···N hydrogen bond is weaker than O–H···O because nitrogen is less electronegative than oxygen, so amines boil lower than comparable alcohols (e.g. n-butylamine 350.8 K vs butan-1-ol 390.3 K). NCERT gives benzoylation: CH₃NH₂ + C₆H₅COCl → C₆H₅CONHCH₃ + HCl.
steps: Statement I: weaker H-bonding in amines → true
Statement II: benzoylation gives N-methylbenzamide → true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', physical properties; chemical reactions (benzoylation)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): An aqueous solution of methylamine gives a precipitate of ferric hydroxide with FeCl₃ solution.
Reason (R): Methylamine is a base; in water it accepts a proton and produces hydroxide ions.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Basicity of aliphatic amines in water
solution.explanation: CH₃NH₂ + H₂O ⇌ CH₃NH₃⁺ + OH⁻. The hydroxide ions precipitate Fe³⁺ as hydrated ferric oxide: Fe³⁺ + 3OH⁻ → Fe(OH)₃.
steps: A: brown precipitate of Fe(OH)₃ → true
R: CH₃NH₂ produces OH⁻ in water → true
The OH⁻ produced is what precipitates Fe(OH)₃ → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', basic character of amines
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the amine in List-I with its IUPAC name in List-II.

List-I:
A. C₆H₅N(CH₃)₂
B. CH₃CH₂NHCH₃
C. (C₂H₅)₃N
D. H₂N–CH₂–CH₂–NH₂

List-II:
I. Ethane-1,2-diamine
II. N,N-Diethylethanamine
III. N-Methylethanamine
IV. N,N-Dimethylbenzenamine

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The longest alkyl chain (or benzene) gives the parent amine; other groups on nitrogen are cited with the locant N. A diamine gets the suffix -diamine with the locants of both nitrogen-bearing carbons.
steps: A: benzenamine with two N-methyls → N,N-dimethylbenzenamine (IV)
B: ethanamine with one N-methyl → N-methylethanamine (III)
C: ethanamine with two N-ethyls → N,N-diethylethanamine (II)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', nomenclature
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the basic strength of amines are correct?

(a) In aqueous solution, the basic strength of an amine is decided by the combination of the inductive effect, solvation and steric hindrance of the alkyl groups.
(b) The larger the Kb of an amine, the weaker it is as a base.
(c) The smaller the pKb of an amine, the stronger it is as a base.
(d) Bulky alkyl groups on nitrogen hinder the hydrogen bonding (solvation) of the substituted ammonium ion with water, which lowers the basic strength.
(e) Among the ethyl-substituted amines in water, triethylamine is the strongest base.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Basicity of amines: Kb, pKb and the factors involved
solution.explanation: A larger Kb (smaller pKb) means a stronger base. In water, +I effect, solvation of the ammonium ion and steric hindrance together decide basicity; for the ethyl series the order is (C₂H₅)₂NH > (C₂H₅)₃N > C₂H₅NH₂ > NH₃.
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option includes (b) or (e), both false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', basic character of amines (structure–basicity relationship)
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
In the Hofmann bromamide degradation,
RCONH₂ + Br₂ + 4NaOH → RNH₂ + Na₂CO₃ + 2NaBr + 2H₂O
the minimum mass of NaOH needed to convert 5.9 g of ethanamide completely into methanamine is (C = 12, H = 1, N = 14, O = 16, Na = 23):

solution.concept: Stoichiometry of the Hofmann bromamide reaction
solution.explanation: Four moles of NaOH are used per mole of amide (to form NaBr, Na₂CO₃ and to neutralise the reaction intermediates).
solution.why_others_wrong: 4.0 g, 8.0 g and 12.0 g take 1, 2 or 3 mol of NaOH per mole of amide instead of the 4 shown in the balanced equation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', preparation of amines (Hofmann bromamide degradation)
solution.final_answer: Option D: 16.0 g

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 9.3 g of aniline is acetylated with ethanoic anhydride; the product is brominated with Br₂ in ethanoic acid to give the para-bromo compound, which is then hydrolysed. Assuming every step is complete, the mass of the final product is (C = 12, H = 1, N = 14, O = 16, Br = 80):

solution.concept: Controlling the reactivity of aniline by acetylation
solution.explanation: Acetylation moderates the activating –NH₂ group so that only monobromination occurs (at the para position). Hydrolysis then removes the acetyl group, giving 4-bromoaniline.
solution.why_others_wrong: 13.5 g is the mass of acetanilide and 21.4 g that of p-bromoacetanilide (the steps before hydrolysis). 33.0 g is 2,4,6-tribromoaniline, formed only if aniline itself is brominated.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', electrophilic substitution (bromination of aniline via acetanilide)
solution.final_answer: Option B: 17.2 g

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Ethanol reduces benzenediazonium chloride to benzene.
Reason (R): In this reaction, ethanol is oxidised to ethanoic acid.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Replacement of the diazo group by hydrogen
solution.explanation: Mild reducing agents such as hypophosphorous acid or ethanol replace –N₂⁺ by –H. NCERT's equation: ArN₂⁺Cl⁻ + CH₃CH₂OH → ArH + N₂ + CH₃CHO + HCl. Ethanol is oxidised only to ethanal.
steps: R: the oxidation product is ethanal, not ethanoic acid → false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', reactions of diazonium salts (replacement by hydrogen)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Commercially, glucose is obtained by boiling which substance with dilute H₂SO₄ at 393 K under 2–3 bar pressure?

solution.explanation: NCERT: glucose is obtained commercially by hydrolysis of starch: (C₆H₁₀O₅)ₙ + nH₂O → nC₆H₁₂O₆ (dilute H₂SO₄, 393 K, 2–3 bar). In the laboratory it is made by boiling sucrose with dilute acid, which gives glucose and fructose.
solution.why_others_wrong: Sucrose hydrolysis is the laboratory method and also gives fructose. Lactose gives galactose as well. Cellulose is not the commercial source NCERT describes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', preparation of glucose
solution.final_answer: Option A: Starch

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the vitamin in List-I with a source of it in List-II.

List-I:
A. Vitamin D
B. Vitamin E
C. Vitamin C
D. Vitamin B₁₂

List-II:
I. Citrus fruits, amla and green leafy vegetables
II. Exposure to sunlight; fish and egg yolk
III. Meat, fish, egg and curd
IV. Vegetable oils such as wheat germ oil and sunflower oil

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: From NCERT's table: vitamin D – exposure to sunlight, fish and egg yolk; vitamin E – vegetable oils like wheat germ oil and sunflower oil; vitamin C – citrus fruits, amla and green leafy vegetables; vitamin B₁₂ – meat, fish, egg and curd.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', vitamins (sources and deficiency diseases table)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Amylose is insoluble in water, whereas amylopectin is water soluble.
Statement II: Cellulose is a branched-chain polymer of β-D-glucose units.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: amylose is the water-soluble component of starch (15–20%) and amylopectin is insoluble in water. Cellulose is a straight-chain polysaccharide of β-D-glucose units joined by C1–C4 glycosidic linkages.
steps: Statement II: cellulose is unbranched → false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', polysaccharides
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In a sample of double-stranded DNA, 20% of the bases are adenine. The percentage of cytosine is:

solution.explanation: In double-stranded DNA, adenine pairs with thymine and guanine with cytosine, so A = T and G = C.
solution.why_others_wrong: 20% equates cytosine with adenine. 60% is G + C together. 40% is A + T.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', structure of nucleic acids (base pairing)
solution.final_answer: Option D: 30%

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In a nucleoside, the base is attached to the pentose sugar at its:

solution.explanation: NCERT: a unit formed by the attachment of a base to the 1′ position of the sugar is a nucleoside. When the 5′ position of the sugar carries a phosphate, the unit is a nucleotide.
solution.why_others_wrong: The 5′ position carries the phosphate in a nucleotide, and 3′ and 5′ are joined in the phosphodiester links of the chain. The 2′ position differs between ribose (OH) and deoxyribose (H).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', chemical composition and structure of nucleic acids
solution.final_answer: Option B: 1′ position

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Almost all enzymes are globular proteins.
Reason (R): Enzymes are very specific for a particular reaction and for a particular substrate.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Both statements are NCERT facts about enzymes. That enzymes are proteins with a globular shape does not follow from their specificity, and their specificity is not why they are proteins, so R does not explain A.
steps: A: enzymes are biocatalysts, almost all globular proteins → true
R describes a different property → not the explanation
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', enzymes
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about nucleic acids are correct?

(a) The double-helix structure of DNA was proposed by James Watson and Francis Crick.
(b) In nucleic acids, nucleotides are joined by phosphodiester linkages between the 5′ and 3′ carbon atoms of the pentose sugars.
(c) DNA contains uracil.
(d) Adenine and guanine are pyrimidine bases.
(e) The sugar in RNA lacks an –OH group at the 2′ position.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Watson and Crick proposed the double helix; nucleotides are linked by 5′–3′ phosphodiester bonds. DNA contains A, G, C and T (uracil occurs in RNA instead of thymine). Adenine and guanine are purines; cytosine, thymine and uracil are pyrimidines. Ribose in RNA has a 2′-OH; deoxyribose in DNA lacks it.
steps: (d) A and G are purines → false
(e) it is deoxyribose (DNA) that lacks the 2′-OH → false
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option includes (c), (d) or (e), all false, or leaves out (a) or (b).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', nucleic acids
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a) and (b) only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 8.1 g of a polysaccharide (C₆H₁₀O₅)ₙ is hydrolysed completely to glucose, and all the glucose is fermented: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂. The volume of CO₂ at STP is (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16; molar volume at STP = 22.4 L mol⁻¹):

solution.concept: Hydrolysis of a polysaccharide and fermentation of glucose
solution.explanation: Each C₆H₁₀O₅ unit (162 g mol⁻¹) gives one glucose molecule on hydrolysis, and each glucose gives two CO₂.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1.12 L takes one CO₂ per glucose. 4.48 L doubles again. 2.02 L uses 180 g mol⁻¹ (glucose) instead of 162 g mol⁻¹ for the polysaccharide unit.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', polysaccharides; Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', ethanol by fermentation
solution.final_answer: Option A: 2.24 L

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: A protein found in a biological system with a unique three-dimensional structure and biological activity is called a native protein.
Statement II: The main forces that stabilise the secondary and tertiary structures of proteins are hydrogen bonds, disulphide linkages, van der Waals forces and electrostatic forces of attraction.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Native proteins and the forces that stabilise protein structure
solution.explanation: Both are NCERT statements. When these stabilising interactions are disturbed (by heat or change of pH), the protein loses its biological activity: denaturation.
steps: Statement I: definition of native protein → true
Statement II: true as NCERT lists them
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', structure of proteins; denaturation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the amino acid in List-I with its one-letter code in List-II.

List-I:
A. Lysine
B. Phenylalanine
C. Tyrosine
D. Tryptophan

List-II:
I. Y
II. W
III. K
IV. F

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT's table of amino acids gives: lysine K, phenylalanine F, tyrosine Y, tryptophan W (the first letters L, P and T belong to leucine, proline and threonine).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', amino acids (table of natural amino acids)
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A ferric hydroxide sol is prepared by adding ferric chloride solution drop by drop to:

solution.concept: Preparation of a lyophobic sol by hydrolysis
solution.explanation: FeCl₃ is hydrolysed in boiling water: FeCl₃ + 3H₂O → Fe(OH)₃ (sol) + 3HCl, giving a reddish-brown sol. The Fe(OH)₃ particles adsorb Fe³⁺ ions, which keep the sol stable.
steps: Add FeCl₃ dropwise to boiling water
solution.why_others_wrong: In cold water hydrolysis is too slow. NaOH or NH₄OH solution gives a precipitate of Fe(OH)₃, not a sol.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), preparation of lyophobic sols (ferric hydroxide)
solution.final_answer: Option B: boiling distilled water

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The volume of 0.10 M oxalic acid solution needed to prepare 250 mL of 0.020 M oxalic acid solution by dilution is:

solution.explanation: The number of moles of solute does not change on dilution.
steps: V₁ = 50 mL (made up to 250 mL with water)
solution.why_others_wrong: 200 mL is the water added, not the volume of stock solution. 1250 mL inverts the ratio of molarities. 5.0 mL uses 1.0 M for the stock solution.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), titrimetric analysis (preparation of standard solutions)
solution.final_answer: Option C: 50 mL

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Starch forms a lyophilic sol when warmed and stirred with water.
Statement II: Arsenious sulphide forms a lyophilic sol.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Starch, gum and egg albumin form lyophilic (solvent-loving) sols directly with water. Arsenious sulphide sol is lyophobic; it is prepared by a chemical reaction (double decomposition of As₂O₃ with H₂S).
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), preparation of lyophilic and lyophobic sols
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 13.5 g of acetanilide is nitrated to p-nitroacetanilide, and the yield of the purified product is 70%. The mass of p-nitroacetanilide obtained is (C = 12, H = 1, N = 14, O = 16):

solution.concept: Percentage yield in a laboratory preparation
solution.explanation: C₆H₅NHCOCH₃ + HNO₃ → p-O₂NC₆H₄NHCOCH₃ + H₂O; one mole of acetanilide gives at most one mole of product.
solution.why_others_wrong: 18.0 g is the theoretical (100%) yield. 9.45 g takes 70% of the mass of acetanilide. 9.66 g is 70% of 0.10 mol of p-nitroaniline, the product after hydrolysis, which is not formed here.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), preparation of p-nitroacetanilide
solution.final_answer: Option D: 12.6 g

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Detection of elements and functional groups
questions.question_text:
Match the substance or group in List-I with the observation in its laboratory test in List-II.

List-I:
A. Carbohydrate (Molisch's test)
B. Oil or fat (heating with KHSO₄)
C. Protein (ninhydrin test)
D. Ketone (sodium nitroprusside test)

List-II:
I. Violet ring at the junction of the two layers
II. Blue-violet colour
III. Red colour in alkaline solution
IV. Pungent smell of acrolein

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Tests for carbohydrates, fats, proteins and ketones
solution.explanation: Molisch's test (α-naphthol, then conc. H₂SO₄ down the side) gives a violet ring for carbohydrates. Heating a fat or oil with KHSO₄ gives acrolein, with a pungent smell. Ninhydrin gives a blue-violet colour with proteins (amino acids). Ketones such as propanone give a red colour with sodium nitroprusside in alkali.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), tests for carbohydrates, fats and proteins; tests for functional groups
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-I, B-IV, C-II, D-III

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A solution contains both oxalic acid and sodium oxalate. 25.0 mL of it needs 20.0 mL of 0.10 M NaOH for neutralisation (phenolphthalein). Another 25.0 mL portion, acidified with dilute H₂SO₄ and warmed, needs 40.0 mL of 0.020 M KMnO₄. The molarity of sodium oxalate in the solution is:

solution.concept: Combining an acid–base titration with a redox titration
solution.explanation: Only oxalic acid (dibasic) reacts with NaOH, but both oxalic acid and oxalate ions are oxidised by permanganate (2MnO₄⁻ : 5C₂O₄²⁻).
steps: Sodium oxalate = 2.0 − 1.0 = 1.0 mmol in 25.0 mL → 0.040 M
solution.why_others_wrong: 0.080 M is the total oxalate (oxalic acid not subtracted). 0.120 M adds the oxalic acid instead of subtracting it. 0.024 M takes the MnO₄⁻ : C₂O₄²⁻ ratio as 1 : 2.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), titrimetric analysis (oxalic acid against NaOH and against KMnO₄)
solution.final_answer: Option B: 0.040 M

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following observations in salt analysis are correctly described?

(a) Al³⁺: the white gelatinous precipitate of group III, dissolved in dilute HCl and treated with blue litmus and NH₄OH, gives a blue 'lake'.
(b) Mg²⁺ is precipitated in group V by ammonium carbonate in the presence of NH₄Cl and NH₄OH.
(c) Zn²⁺ is precipitated in group IV as a black sulphide.
(d) A nitrite gives brown fumes when warmed with dilute H₂SO₄.
(e) A phosphate gives a yellow precipitate when heated with concentrated HNO₃ and ammonium molybdate.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Identification of cations and anions in salt analysis
solution.explanation: Al(OH)₃ adsorbs litmus to give a blue lake. Mg²⁺ is not precipitated in group V (the NH₄⁺ salts keep MgCO₃ in solution); it is detected in group VI with disodium hydrogen phosphate. ZnS is white (MnS buff, NiS and CoS black). Nitrite gives brown NO₂ with dilute acid (nitrate needs concentrated acid). Phosphate gives yellow ammonium phosphomolybdate.
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option includes (b) or (c), both false.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), systematic qualitative analysis of cations and anions
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (d) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In which of the following pairs of organisms does NCERT describe asexual reproduction by budding?

solution.concept: Reproduction as a feature of living organisms
solution.explanation: NCERT notes that organisms reproduce asexually in different ways: in yeast and Hydra we observe budding, while in Planaria (flatworms) we observe true regeneration. Fungi, filamentous algae and the protonema of mosses multiply by fragmentation.
steps: Fragmentation → fungi, filamentous algae, protonema of mosses
solution.why_others_wrong: Planaria is NCERT's example of true regeneration, not budding. Fungi, filamentous algae and the moss protonema are its examples of fragmentation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'The Living World', Diversity in the Living World (characteristics of living organisms)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Yeast and Hydra

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The capsid of a virus is made of small subunits called capsomeres. NCERT states that the capsomeres are arranged in:

options.text: two thin overlapping shells that fit like a soap box
stiff cellulose plates on the outer surface
a flexible protein-rich layer called the pellicle

solution.explanation: A virus has a protein coat, the capsid, made of small subunits called capsomeres, which protects the nucleic acid. The capsomeres are arranged in helical or polyhedral geometric forms.
solution.why_others_wrong: Two overlapping shells describe the diatom wall, cellulose plates the wall of dinoflagellates, and the pellicle the body covering of euglenoids.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Viruses, Viroids, Prions and Lichens
solution.final_answer: Option C: helical or polyhedral geometric forms

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The word 'systematics' is derived from the Latin word 'systema', which means:

options.text: naming of organisms with two words
grouping of organisms by their mode of nutrition
the study of the evolutionary history of organisms

solution.explanation: The word systematics is derived from the Latin word 'systema', which means systematic arrangement of organisms. Linnaeus used 'Systema Naturae' as the title of his publication.
solution.why_others_wrong: Two-word naming is binomial nomenclature. Mode of nutrition is only one criterion of Whittaker's classification. Systematics takes evolutionary relationships into account, but that is not the meaning of 'systema'.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'The Living World', Diversity in the Living World (systematics)
solution.final_answer: Option B: systematic arrangement of organisms

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Fungi are cosmopolitan and occur in air, water, soil and on animals and plants.
Statement II: Fungi that absorb soluble organic matter from dead substrates are called parasites.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Fungi are cosmopolitan and occur in air, water, soil and on animals and plants. Most fungi are heterotrophic and absorb soluble organic matter from dead substrates; these are called saprophytes. Those that depend on living plants and animals are called parasites.
steps: Statement II: false, fungi living on dead substrates are saprophytes
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Fungi
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which class of fungi is commonly known as the sac-fungi?

solution.explanation: Commonly known as sac-fungi, the ascomycetes are mostly multicellular, e.g., Penicillium, or rarely unicellular, e.g., yeast (Saccharomyces). Their sexual spores, ascospores, are produced in sac-like asci.
solution.why_others_wrong: Phycomycetes are the algal fungi with aseptate mycelium. Basidiomycetes are the mushrooms, bracket fungi and puffballs. Deuteromycetes are the imperfect fungi.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Fungi (Ascomycetes)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Ascomycetes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (group of protists) with List-II (habitat or habit).

List-I:
A. Chrysophytes
B. Dinoflagellates
C. Euglenoids
D. Slime moulds

List-II:
I. Mostly marine and photosynthetic; appear yellow, green, brown, blue or red
II. Majority are fresh-water organisms found in stagnant water
III. Body moves along decaying twigs and leaves, engulfing organic material
IV. Found in fresh water as well as marine environments; float passively in water currents (plankton)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Chrysophytes (diatoms and desmids) occur in fresh water as well as marine environments and float passively as plankton. Dinoflagellates are mostly marine and photosynthetic, and appear yellow, green, brown, blue or red depending on their pigments. The majority of euglenoids are fresh-water organisms of stagnant water. Slime moulds are saprophytic protists whose body moves along decaying twigs and leaves, engulfing organic material.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap chrysophytes with dinoflagellates (both photosynthetic, but only dinoflagellates are mostly marine), or euglenoids with slime moulds (only slime moulds engulf decaying organic matter).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Protista
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Viruses are obligate parasites.
Reason (R): Viruses replicate with their own cellular machinery, without needing a host cell.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT describes viruses as obligate parasites: once they infect a cell, they take over the machinery of the host cell to replicate themselves, killing the host. Viruses are not cells and have no machinery of their own, so R is false.
steps: R: false, viruses use the host cell's machinery to replicate
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Viruses, Viroids, Prions and Lichens
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In Whittaker's table of the five kingdoms, the nuclear envelope is absent only in kingdom Monera.
Statement II: In the same table, the body organisation of kingdom Protista is described as cellular.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Table 2.1 of NCERT gives the nuclear envelope as absent in Monera and present in Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia. The body organisation is cellular in Monera and Protista, multicellular/loose tissue in Fungi, tissue/organ in Plantae and tissue/organ/organ system in Animalia.
steps: Statement I: true (Monera is the only prokaryotic kingdom)
Statement II: true (Monera and Protista are both cellular)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Introduction (Table 2.1: Characteristics of the Five Kingdoms)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The fruiting bodies of slime moulds bear spores at their tips. These spores are dispersed by:

options.text: the flagella of the spores themselves
insects that visit the fruiting bodies

solution.explanation: Under unfavourable conditions the plasmodium of a slime mould differentiates and forms fruiting bodies bearing spores at their tips. The spores possess true walls, are extremely resistant, and are dispersed by air currents.
steps: Slime mould spores → dispersed by air currents
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT names only air currents as the agent of dispersal. The spores are walled and do not swim, and insects are not mentioned.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Protista (Slime Moulds)
solution.final_answer: Option D: air currents

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The process by which anything is grouped into convenient categories based on some easily observable characters is called:

solution.explanation: Classification is the process by which anything is grouped into convenient categories based on some easily observable characters. Characterisation, identification, classification and nomenclature together are the processes basic to taxonomy.
solution.why_others_wrong: Identification is recognising an organism correctly, nomenclature is giving it its correct scientific name, and characterisation is describing its characters. None of these is the grouping into categories.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'The Living World', Taxonomic Categories
solution.final_answer: Option A: classification

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Prions are infectious agents consisting of abnormally folded protein, and they are similar in size to viruses.
Statement II: Bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), commonly called mad cow disease, is a prion disease of humans.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Certain infectious neurological diseases are transmitted by an agent consisting of abnormally folded protein, similar in size to viruses; these agents are called prions. BSE (mad cow disease) is a prion disease of cattle; its analogous variant in humans is Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease (CJD).
steps: Statement II: false, BSE occurs in cattle; the human disease is CJD
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Viruses, Viroids, Prions and Lichens
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): There is a need to standardise the naming of living organisms so that a particular organism is known by the same name all over the world.
Reason (R): The local names of plants and animals vary from place to place, even within a country.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: We know plants and animals of our own area by their local names, and these names vary from place to place, even within a country. This creates confusion, so a standardised naming system is needed in which a particular organism has the same name all over the world. R is the reason given for A.
steps: Varying local names cause confusion → need for one standard name → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'The Living World', Diversity in the Living World (nomenclature)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about reproduction in fungi are correct?

(a) The sexual cycle involves plasmogamy, then karyogamy, and then meiosis in the zygote resulting in haploid spores.
(b) In phycomycetes, zygospores are formed by the fusion of two gametes, which may be isogamous, anisogamous or oogamous.
(c) Conidia are the sexual spores of ascomycetes.
(d) Vegetative reproduction in fungi takes place by fragmentation, fission and budding.
(e) Basidiocarps are the fruiting bodies of ascomycetes.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Fungi reproduce vegetatively by fragmentation, fission and budding; asexually by conidia, sporangiospores or zoospores; and sexually by oospores, ascospores and basidiospores. The sexual cycle has three steps: plasmogamy, karyogamy and meiosis in the zygote giving haploid spores. In phycomycetes, zygospores form by fusion of two gametes that are isogamous, anisogamous or oogamous. Conidia are asexual spores; the sexual spores of ascomycetes are ascospores. Basidiocarps are the fruiting bodies of basidiomycetes; those of ascomycetes are ascocarps.
solution.why_others_wrong: (a, b, c) and (b, d, e) include a false statement. (a, d) leaves out the true statement (b).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Fungi
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about members of kingdom Animalia are correct?

(a) They are heterotrophic, eukaryotic, multicellular organisms whose cells lack cell walls.
(b) Their mode of nutrition is holozoic, that is, by ingestion of food.
(c) They follow a definite growth pattern and grow into adults of definite shape and size.
(d) Sexual reproduction is by copulation of male and female followed by embryological development.
(e) They store food reserves mainly as starch.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Animals are heterotrophic, eukaryotic and multicellular, and their cells lack cell walls. They depend directly or indirectly on plants for food, digest food in an internal cavity and store food reserves as glycogen or fat. Nutrition is holozoic. They follow a definite growth pattern, and sexual reproduction is by copulation of male and female followed by embryological development.
steps: (e) false: animals store glycogen or fat, not starch
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (e) include a false statement. (a, b, d) leaves out the true statement (c).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Animalia
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about kingdom Monera are correct?

(a) Cyanobacteria may be unicellular, colonial or filamentous, and may be freshwater, marine or terrestrial.
(b) The colonies of cyanobacteria are generally surrounded by a gelatinous sheath.
(c) Bacteria reproduce mainly by fission and, under unfavourable conditions, may produce spores.
(d) Heterotrophic bacteria are helpful in making curd from milk and in fixing nitrogen in legume roots.
(e) Eubacteria are characterised by the absence of a rigid cell wall.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Cyanobacteria are unicellular, colonial or filamentous, freshwater, marine or terrestrial algae; their colonies are generally surrounded by a gelatinous sheath. Heterotrophic bacteria help in making curd from milk, producing antibiotics and fixing nitrogen in legume roots. Bacteria reproduce mainly by fission and sometimes form spores under unfavourable conditions. True bacteria (eubacteria) are characterised by the presence of a rigid cell wall and, if motile, a flagellum.
steps: (e) false: eubacteria have a rigid cell wall
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (e) include a false statement. (b, c, d) leaves out the true statement (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Monera
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): All fungi are multicellular and filamentous.
Reason (R): Fungi show a great diversity in morphology and habitat.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT states that, with the exception of yeasts, which are unicellular, fungi are filamentous. So A is false. R is true: the fungi form a unique kingdom of heterotrophic organisms that show a great diversity in morphology and habitat.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Fungi
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Before the five kingdom system, bacteria, blue-green algae, fungi, mosses, ferns, gymnosperms and angiosperms were all placed under 'Plants'.
Statement II: Paramoecium and Amoeba, now placed in kingdom Protista, were earlier placed in the animal kingdom and lack a cell wall.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Two kingdom versus five kingdom classification
solution.explanation: The earlier classification placed bacteria, blue-green algae, fungi, mosses, ferns, gymnosperms and angiosperms under 'Plants', the unifying character being a cell wall. Kingdom Protista brought together Chlamydomonas and Chlorella (earlier algae within plants, both with cell walls) with Paramoecium and Amoeba (earlier in the animal kingdom, which lack a cell wall).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Introduction
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The name 'gymnosperm' (Greek gymnos, sperma) refers to plants in which the:

options.text: seeds are enclosed within a fruit
male gametes are naked and swim in water
seeds are naked, that is, not covered
spores are produced in naked cones without sporophylls

solution.explanation: Gymnosperms (gymnos: naked, sperma: seeds) are plants in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilisation. The seeds that develop after fertilisation are not covered, that is, they are naked.
steps: Ovules not enclosed by an ovary wall → naked seeds
solution.why_others_wrong: Seeds enclosed in a fruit describe angiosperms. The name refers to seeds, not to male gametes, and the cones of gymnosperms are made of sporophylls.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Gymnosperms
solution.final_answer: Option C: seeds are naked, that is, not covered

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following is a filamentous alga?

solution.explanation: The form and size of algae are highly variable, ranging from colonial forms like Volvox to filamentous forms like Ulothrix and Spirogyra. Chlamydomonas and Chlorella are unicellular green algae.
solution.why_others_wrong: Volvox is NCERT's example of a colonial alga, and Chlamydomonas and Chlorella are unicellular.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae
solution.final_answer: Option D: Spirogyra

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In bryophytes, the antherozoids are released into water, where they come in contact with the archegonium.
Statement II: In bryophytes, an antherozoid fuses with the egg to produce the zygote.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The antheridium of a bryophyte produces biflagellate antherozoids. These are released into water, where they come in contact with the archegonium. An antherozoid fuses with the egg to produce the zygote, which develops into the sporophyte.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Bryophytes
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following is a pteridophyte?

solution.explanation: NCERT lists Selaginella and Lycopodium (Lycopsida), Equisetum (Sphenopsida), and the ferns Dryopteris, Pteris and Adiantum (Pteropsida) as pteridophytes.
solution.why_others_wrong: Sphagnum is a moss, Gracilaria a red alga and Cedrus a gymnosperm.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Pteridophytes
solution.final_answer: Option B: Dryopteris

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The female sex organ of bryophytes, the archegonium, is:

options.text: pear-shaped and produces many biflagellate gametes
flask-shaped and produces a single egg

solution.explanation: The sex organs of bryophytes are multicellular. The male sex organ, the antheridium, produces biflagellate antherozoids. The female sex organ, the archegonium, is flask-shaped and produces a single egg.
solution.why_others_wrong: Pear-shaped biflagellate cells are the gametes of brown algae. Gemma cups are asexual structures of liverworts. A sac producing spores is a spore-bearing structure, not a sex organ.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Bryophytes
solution.final_answer: Option D: flask-shaped and produces a single egg

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The cells of the nucellus in the ovule of a gymnosperm have 24 chromosomes each. How many chromosomes will be present in the megaspore mother cell, in a cell of the female gametophyte and in a cell of the embryo, respectively?

solution.explanation: The megaspore mother cell is differentiated from one of the cells of the nucellus, so it is diploid (24). It divides meiotically to form four haploid megaspores; one of them develops into the multicellular female gametophyte, whose cells are haploid (12). The zygote formed after fertilisation is diploid and develops into the embryo (24).
solution.why_others_wrong: 12, 12 and 24 treats the megaspore mother cell as already haploid. 24, 24 and 24 forgets that meiosis precedes the female gametophyte. 24, 12 and 12 forgets that fertilisation restores the diploid number in the embryo.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Gymnosperms
solution.final_answer: Option C: 24, 12 and 24

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The needle-like leaves of conifers help to reduce water loss.
Reason (R): Needle-like leaves have a reduced surface area.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The leaves of gymnosperms are well adapted to withstand extremes of temperature, humidity and wind. In conifers, the needle-like leaves reduce the surface area, and their thick cuticle and sunken stomata also help to reduce water loss. A smaller surface area directly means less surface for water loss, so R explains A.
steps: Less surface area → less water lost → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Gymnosperms
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In Chlorophyceae, asexual reproduction is by flagellated zoospores produced in zoosporangia.
Statement II: In most members of Chlorophyceae, the storage bodies called pyrenoids are located in the cell wall.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: In green algae, asexual reproduction is by flagellated zoospores produced in zoosporangia. Most members have one or more storage bodies called pyrenoids, located in the chloroplasts; pyrenoids contain protein besides starch.
steps: Statement II: false, pyrenoids are located in the chloroplasts
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae (Chlorophyceae)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following features is shared by pteridophytes and gymnosperms but NOT by bryophytes?

options.text: Water is required for the transfer of male gametes to the archegonium
The main plant body is a sporophyte with vascular tissues (xylem and phloem)
The gametophyte has an independent, free-living existence

solution.explanation: In bryophytes the main plant body is the haploid gametophyte and vascular tissue is absent. Pteridophytes are the first terrestrial plants to possess xylem and phloem, and in them, as in gymnosperms, the main plant body is the sporophyte.
steps: Bryophytes: gametophyte dominant, no vascular tissue
Pteridophytes and gymnosperms: sporophyte dominant, vascular tissue present
solution.why_others_wrong: Water for fertilisation and a free-living gametophyte are shared by bryophytes and pteridophytes, not gymnosperms. Seeds are formed by gymnosperms but not by pteridophytes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Bryophytes; Pteridophytes; Gymnosperms
solution.final_answer: Option B: The main plant body is a sporophyte with vascular tissues (xylem and phloem)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The cell wall contains cellulose in members of both Phaeophyceae and Rhodophyceae.
Statement II: Algin and carrageen are hydrocolloids, that is, water-holding substances.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Cell walls and products of algae
solution.explanation: Table 3.1 gives the cell wall of Phaeophyceae as cellulose and algin, and that of Rhodophyceae as cellulose, pectin and polysulphate esters. Certain marine brown and red algae produce large amounts of hydrocolloids (water-holding substances), e.g., algin (brown algae) and carrageen (red algae), which are used commercially.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae (Table 3.1)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a brown alga?

solution.explanation: NCERT gives Ectocarpus, Dictyota, Laminaria, Sargassum and Fucus as examples of brown algae (Phaeophyceae). Gracilaria, with Gelidium, is a red alga from which agar is obtained.
steps: Brown algae: Ectocarpus, Dictyota, Laminaria, Sargassum, Fucus
solution.why_others_wrong: Dictyota, Laminaria and Sargassum are all listed by NCERT as members of Phaeophyceae.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae (Phaeophyceae; Rhodophyceae)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Gracilaria

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Members of Chlorophyceae are usually grass green in colour.
Reason (R): In members of Chlorophyceae, the pigments chlorophyll a and b are dominant.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT states that members of Chlorophyceae are usually grass green due to the dominance of the pigments chlorophyll a and b. The dominant pigments decide the colour, so R explains A.
steps: Dominant chlorophyll a and b → grass green → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae (Chlorophyceae)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements comparing bryophytes, pteridophytes and gymnosperms are correct?

(a) Archegonia are formed in all three groups.
(b) Vascular tissues are present in pteridophytes and gymnosperms but absent in bryophytes.
(c) Water is required for fertilisation in both bryophytes and pteridophytes.
(d) A free-living gametophyte is found in all three groups.
(e) Seeds are formed in both pteridophytes and gymnosperms.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Comparison of bryophytes, pteridophytes and gymnosperms
solution.explanation: Archegonia occur in bryophytes, on the prothallus of pteridophytes, and on the female gametophyte of gymnosperms (two or more per gametophyte). Vascular tissue first appears in pteridophytes. In bryophytes the antherozoids are released into water, and in pteridophytes water is required to carry antherozoids to the archegonium. The gametophytes of gymnosperms are not free-living, and seeds are formed only in gymnosperms.
steps: (d) false: gymnosperm gametophytes are not free-living
(e) false: pteridophytes do not form seeds
solution.why_others_wrong: (a, b, d) and (b, c, e) contain a false statement. (a, c) leaves out the true statement (b).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Bryophytes; Pteridophytes; Gymnosperms
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following algae are correctly matched with their class?

(a) Laminaria – Phaeophyceae
(b) Gelidium – Rhodophyceae
(c) Chara – Chlorophyceae
(d) Fucus – Rhodophyceae
(e) Volvox – Phaeophyceae

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Laminaria and Fucus are brown algae (Phaeophyceae). Gelidium is a red alga (Rhodophyceae). Chara and Volvox are green algae (Chlorophyceae).
steps: (d) wrong: Fucus is a brown alga
(e) wrong: Volvox is a green alga
solution.why_others_wrong: Every wrong option includes (d) or (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Mosses, along with lichens, are of great ecological importance in the colonisation of rocks.
Reason (R): Mosses decompose rocks, making the substrate suitable for the growth of higher plants.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Mosses along with lichens are the first organisms to colonise rocks and hence are of great ecological importance. They decompose rocks, making the substrate suitable for the growth of higher plants. Preparing the rock surface for later plants is the reason for their ecological importance, so R explains A.
steps: Rock decomposition prepares the substrate → ecological importance → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Bryophytes
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In algae, the most common asexual spores are zoospores, which are flagellated and on germination give rise to new plants.
Statement II: Sargassum, a seaweed used as food, belongs to Rhodophyceae.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Algae reproduce asexually by different types of spores, the most common being zoospores, which are flagellated (motile) and on germination give rise to new plants. Sargassum, like Laminaria, is a brown alga (Phaeophyceae); many species of Porphyra, Laminaria and Sargassum are used as food.
steps: Statement II: false, Sargassum is a brown alga
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In which of the following pairs is the main plant body a sporophyte with true roots, stem and leaves, while the gametophyte is a small, free-living, photosynthetic thallus?

solution.explanation: In pteridophytes the main plant body is a sporophyte differentiated into true root, stem and leaves. Their spores germinate to give rise to small, multicellular, free-living, mostly photosynthetic thalloid gametophytes called prothallus. Adiantum (a fern) and Equisetum are pteridophytes.
steps: Dominant sporophyte + free-living thalloid gametophyte → pteridophytes
solution.why_others_wrong: Funaria and Marchantia are bryophytes, whose main plant body is the gametophyte. Cycas and Pinus are gymnosperms, whose gametophytes are not free-living. Chara and Volvox are green algae.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Pteridophytes
solution.final_answer: Option B: Adiantum and Equisetum

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A flower that cannot be divided into two similar halves by any vertical plane passing through the centre is called asymmetric (irregular). NCERT's example of such a flower is:

solution.explanation: A flower is actinomorphic when any radial plane through the centre divides it into two similar halves (e.g., mustard, datura, chilli), zygomorphic when only one particular vertical plane does so (e.g., pea, gulmohur, bean, Cassia), and asymmetric (irregular) when no vertical plane through the centre does so, as in canna.
steps: No plane of symmetry → asymmetric → canna
solution.why_others_wrong: Mustard and datura are actinomorphic, and pea is zygomorphic.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Flower
solution.final_answer: Option D: canna

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (member of Solanaceae) with List-II (use).

List-I:
A. Chilli
B. Ashwagandha
C. Brinjal
D. Petunia

List-II:
I. Ornamental
II. Food
III. Spice
IV. Medicine

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Many plants of Solanaceae are sources of food (tomato, brinjal, potato), spice (chilli), medicine (belladonna, ashwagandha), fumigatory (tobacco) and ornamentals (petunia).
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap chilli with ashwagandha, brinjal with petunia, or ashwagandha with brinjal.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Solanaceae (Economic importance)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In some leguminous plants the leaf base becomes swollen. This swollen leaf base is called the:

solution.explanation: A typical leaf has a leaf base, a petiole and a lamina. The leaf base may bear two lateral small leaf-like structures called stipules. In monocotyledons the leaf base expands into a sheath, and in some leguminous plants the leaf base may become swollen; this is called the pulvinus.
solution.why_others_wrong: Stipules are small leaf-like outgrowths of the leaf base. A sheath is the expanded leaf base of monocots. The rachis is the common axis of a pinnately compound leaf.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Leaf
solution.final_answer: Option B: pulvinus

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In parallel venation, the veins run parallel to each other within the lamina.
Statement II: Leaves of most monocotyledons have reticulate venation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The arrangement of veins and veinlets in the lamina is venation. When the veinlets form a network, the venation is reticulate; when the veins run parallel to each other within the lamina, it is parallel. Leaves of dicotyledons generally possess reticulate venation, while parallel venation is characteristic of most monocotyledons.
steps: Statement II: false, most monocots have parallel venation
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Leaf (Venation)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The four whorls of a typical flower are arranged successively on the swollen end of the stalk or pedicel. This swollen end is called the:

solution.explanation: A typical flower has four whorls, calyx, corolla, androecium and gynoecium, arranged successively on the swollen end of the stalk or pedicel, called the thalamus or receptacle.
steps: Swollen end of the pedicel = thalamus (receptacle)
solution.why_others_wrong: The placenta is the cushion-like tissue in the ovary bearing ovules. The pulvinus is a swollen leaf base. The peduncle is the axis of an inflorescence, not the swollen end of the pedicel.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Flower
solution.final_answer: Option D: thalamus or receptacle

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (type of aestivation) with List-II (example).

List-I:
A. Valvate
B. Twisted
C. Imbricate
D. Vexillary

List-II:
I. Bean
II. Gulmohur
III. Calotropis
IV. Cotton

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: In valvate aestivation, sepals or petals just touch one another at the margins (Calotropis). In twisted aestivation, one margin of each appendage overlaps the next (china rose, lady's finger, cotton). In imbricate aestivation, the margins overlap but not in any particular direction (Cassia, gulmohur). In vexillary aestivation, the large standard overlaps the two wings, which overlap the keel (pea, bean).
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap Calotropis with cotton, bean with gulmohur, or cotton with gulmohur.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Flower (Aestivation)
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The family Liliaceae is a characteristic representative of monocotyledonous plants.
Reason (R): Members of Liliaceae have leaves with reticulate venation.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Liliaceae, commonly called the lily family, is a characteristic representative of monocotyledonous plants. Its leaves are mostly basal, alternate, linear and exstipulate, with parallel venation, not reticulate.
steps: R: false, Liliaceae leaves have parallel venation
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Liliaceae
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In Solanaceae, the corolla has five united petals with valvate aestivation.
Statement II: In Solanaceae, the placenta is swollen and bears many ovules.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: In Solanaceae, the corolla has five united petals with valvate aestivation. The gynoecium is bicarpellary, obliquely placed and syncarpous; the ovary is superior and bilocular, and the placenta is swollen with many ovules (axile placentation).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Solanaceae (Floral characters)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following members of Fabaceae is named by NCERT as an ornamental plant?

solution.explanation: Fabaceae members are sources of pulses, edible oil (soyabean, groundnut), dye (Indigofera), fibres (sunhemp), fodder (Sesbania, Trifolium), ornamentals (lupin, sweet pea) and medicine (muliathi).
solution.why_others_wrong: Muliathi is medicinal, sunhemp gives fibre and Indigofera gives dye.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Fabaceae (Economic importance)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Sweet pea

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about flowers are correct?

(a) A flower having both androecium and gynoecium is bisexual.
(b) A flower having either only stamens or only carpels is unisexual.
(c) Mustard and datura have actinomorphic flowers.
